introduction.text: The Arch of Gallienus, located in Rome, is a surviving gate of the ancient Servian Wall that was later expanded and rededicated in the 3rd century AD. It illustrates the evolution of Roman defensive architecture and commemorates Emperor Gallienus.

history.description: The gate was originally part of the Servian Wall, traditionally attributed to the 6th century BC but modern scholarship places its construction in the 4th century BC.
The original arch was built in the 1st century AD.
In 262 AD, the arch was expanded to a triple arch structure and rededicated as the Arch of Gallienus.

design.description: The gate originally consisted of a single arch, now the only surviving element.
The 262 AD expansion added two additional arches, creating a triple arch with a peak height of 8.8 m.
